action: Upgrade Ruby to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and get no fix, so move off them.
date_note: Date of the ruby-lang.org advisory (its history line says originally published 2026-11-19 00:00 UTC).
exec: Seven memory-corruption flaws in Ruby's regex and string handling are fixed; six may allow remote code execution, so apps on older Ruby versions are exposed.
geo_basis: country approximate; the advisory states no place
plain: The Ruby language project fixed seven memory-safety bugs in how Ruby handles text patterns and strings. Six of them may let an attacker run code. Updating Ruby is the fix.

report.note: ruby-lang.org advisory read in full; the iThome article returned 403 and was not read.

summary: The Ruby project's advisory lists seven vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion, fixed in Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. All are memory-corruption bugs (heap buffer overflows, a double free, out-of-bounds reads). The advisory says six may allow remote code execution; the seventh may disclose memory or crash the process. CVE identifiers have been requested.
title: Ruby fixes seven memory-safety flaws in Regexp and String, six possibly allowing code execution

validation.note: Primary source: the Ruby project's own advisory. iThome Taiwan also reported it but returned 403 and was not read.
